💡 Quick summary

A firsthand account from the 2026 Esri User Conference in San Diego highlights the importance of hands-on GIS experience, from data collection to finished maps, and the growing connection between R statistical computing and ArcGIS.

📌 Key takeaways

  • The 2026 Esri User Conference in San Diego featured hands-on labs where participants worked directly with GIS and mapping tools
  • The author's key takeaway: the map we see is only one part of a larger process—Data → Analysis → Map → Understanding
  • R and ArcGIS integration was highlighted as a powerful approach for environmental research, connecting statistical patterns to geographic locations
  • GIS transforms spreadsheet data (e.g., water quality measurements) into spatial information linked to lakes, rivers, watersheds, and communities
  • Understanding how tools contribute to answering questions matters more than mastering individual software commands
